how: A participant proposes orange lettering, while the joining response belongs separately to acceptance of the proposal.
Build requests locate the work and renew recruitment when people damage the oil drop.
Members answer proposals with short offers to place pixels or help the logo.
Members propose a droplet mockup, call for a design-switch vote and continue debating the logo shape.
Progress reports describe taking shape, random blocks and unfinished parts of the mark.
A shared font, an anchor-coordinate answer and alignment instructions give placers common references.
Upkeep includes explicit maintenance priorities, overnight protection and calls to patch damage.
Participants attribute displacement to CSGO bots and later destruction to the Void without independently identifying every placer.
Members spare a rival to avoid retaliation and refuse invasion because they disliked experiencing it themselves.
A proposed truce receives explicit acceptance of a defence pact.
Attack calls seek a rival logo's destruction or recolouring, and a participant reports repeated timer-guided blue placement.
A bot attack explicitly explains displacement and a subsequent instruction locates the renewed attempt.
Members thank the group for bonding and credit those replacing pixels until the finish.
Mourning, screenshots, an explanatory video and an ending announcement record the mark's fate.
Continuation takes the minimal form of hoping for better luck and promising to defend when the event returns.
Members criticize scripting, report its use and penalties, and provide a maintenance script.
Mutual defence is requested and a participant later reports a limited period of defending the rival mark.
A defence pact becomes a shared regional section and an alignment against the Void.
Members celebrate a rival's damaged mark, blame the Void and angrily reject another collaboration.
Adjacent marks and mutual protection do not establish guest construction under host jurisdiction.
A narrow surviving canvas title and an ordinary shitpost's reported sanctions cannot establish canvas-specific boundary rules or their rationale.
Repudiating future collaboration and limiting personal help do not explicitly establish who could bind the room or whether the pact bound placers.
An author corrects perceived non-survival by claiming the oil drop remains visible, while the actual image and final-cut authority remain unverifiable.
A maintenance script and a promise to notify another subreddit do not establish planning in a chat.
Members explain access before placement and the timer and collaboration after closure, without requiring a recruiting effect.
Visitors identify ordinary hockey connections without saying a canvas mark brought them into the room.
Members turn canvas loss into team-history jokes and imagine a mocking message that vandals might have written.
The first design proposal chooses an initial location and another suggests available room beside the rival mark.
A pact within an existing community does not establish formation of a new room around a canvas mark.
Objecting to a local takeover joke does not establish a dispute over offensive words or symbols in canvas talk.
Naming the player in a design and recruitment call does not establish seeking acknowledgement from the team or player.
Refusing to inflict a disliked invasion supplies a moral reason against covering another group's work.
Relief at imposed closure and tiredness do not establish voluntary withdrawal under strain or repair of an interpersonal quarrel.
An overt promise to notify the neighbour does not establish hiding plans, infiltrating a rival venue or covert operations.
A complaint about AutoModerator spam does not establish attacking the room's mark because of canvas posts.
Remembering the date and announcing restored moderator control key the separate self-aware-bot performance as April Fools play.
Damage prompts an explicit need for more helpers and a retrospective account explains alliance through insufficient numbers.
A call to recolour the rival logo links the act to an imagined playoff submission.
Participants interpret the canvas predicament through inherited team history and decade-of-darkness language.
Placing costs sleep and competes with work, while later reflection names obsession and tiredness.
Desktop access advice, an official-app alternative and a reported script-related IP block show practical site constraints and fixes.
Defending the ally's logo does not establish membership in both rooms or a stated conflict of belonging.
A proposed vote and conditional assent establish attempted decided order without a completed tally, binding mandate or test of global prevalence.
The same recolouring call explicitly connects the rival canvas mark to a possible hockey playoff confrontation.
A suggestion to tell the neighbouring group receives a promise to comment in its megathread, leaving reception elsewhere unverified.
The game-thread build request receives progress and repair assessments, supporting an answered call without measuring newly recruited placers.
The starter proposal and later recruitment do not establish a distinct starter-to-call causal mechanism.
Members explicitly shift the focus to maintaining the constructed mark and call for continued vigilance.
Truce-making and upkeep are observed without a coded statement identifying neighbouring erosion as the cause of negotiation.
Restraint begins before the pact through anticipated retaliation and aversion to invasion, so an agreed boundary cannot explain its onset.
Upkeep precedes maintenance scripting, but capacity exhaustion as the cause of adoption is not established by the concepts.
Earlier construction and later credit are observed without a concept explicitly connecting a completion report to the decision to celebrate.
Celebration and recording both occur, but the concepts do not establish celebration as the reason for preserving records.
Future-defence wishes occur during recollection without an explicit claim that preserving a record caused the commitment.
Attack explicitly explains moving, while the capacity explanation concerns alliance rather than that relocation.
A mockup precedes the proposed design-switch vote and shape decisions continue later, so a one-way settlement mechanism does not suffice locally.
Bare acceptance is observed alongside a join requesting coordinates and conditional assent, leaving any obligation on every reader unestablished.
Shortage and alliance are explained, but a shortage-driven request cannot be traced to particular returned help.
The pact and later appeals are observed without a coded explanation that border talk opened the channel producing supplied help.
Mobilization can begin as an attack call itself and later recur as a practical recolouring routine.
Invasion proposals receive reasoned refusals grounded in disliked treatment and a distinction between hockey rivalry and canvas vandalism.
Sparing the rival receives the shared alternative of placing a VS between neighbouring marks.
The recolouring call carries hockey rivalry in the same turn, while later Void blame cannot be attributed causally to attacking Calgary.
A participant retrospectively explains alliance as necessary for finishing and protecting marks that smaller groups could not hold alone.
Missing canvas text and ordinary shitpost sanctions leave flood-driven canvas boundary work untestable.
Rejecting future collaboration after closure does not establish a refusal of the operative pact or a statement about its authority over placers.
Maintenance is observed, but planned-change erasure and its cessation after notification cannot be inferred from coded notification proposals alone.
The sole surviving title establishes a canvas topic without announcing that a mark is completed.
Script use includes fairness objections and reported platform penalties rather than uncomplicated capacity escalation.
A defence pact and restraint coexist with repeated individual attacks, so compliance cannot be attributed to every placer.
After cooperation, members repudiate future collaboration, justify the alliance and question or limit a participant's help without explicitly disputing representative authority.
Credit for shared effort continues after final loss and need not depend on an intact mark surviving the close.
Damage to the existing mark directly renews requests for helpers, returning maintenance to mobilization.
Attack-driven relocation is followed by a new anchor-coordinate instruction for trying again.
Interpreting surviving pixels in the final record supplies credit for last-minute defenders and improves the author's feeling about the loss.

statement: Relief at externally imposed closure without voluntary withdrawal
how: Defenders welcome imposed closure while retaining future commitment, which does not establish quitting under stress.

statement: Ordinary team celebration continuing beside canvas work
how: A hockey-record celebration remains ordinary community life rather than evidence of canvas completion.

statement: Ordinary visitor hospitality beside canvas alliances
how: Hockey visitors receive humour, thanks, local advice and viewing help without establishing canvas recruitment or pixel reciprocity.

statement: Ordinary memeing and moderation beside the event
how: An invitation to meme and persistence through sanctions remain ordinary community practices rather than canvas-specific moderation or the staged bot takeover.
